courseTitle: Building Your Second Brain with gbrain
courseDescription: Learn to build a self-improving AI knowledge system that compounds intelligence over time. You'll master the brain-agent loop, compiled truth architecture, and production patterns used in real deployments with 14,000+ brain files — transforming scattered notes into a true external memory.

lessons.title: Compiled Intelligence: Beyond Note-Taking Apps
lessons.learningFocus: Explain the fundamental difference between a notes app and a compiled intelligence system, and describe the two-zone architecture that separates mutable synthesis from immutable evidence.
lessons.openQuestion: If your brain could only keep either the stories you tell yourself OR the raw memories that formed them, which would you choose — and what would you lose?

lessons.title: Your Brain's File System: Directories as Knowledge Graphs
lessons.learningFocus: Navigate and explain gbrain's flat directory structure by entity type, and understand how multiple isolated knowledge repositories (sources) coexist in one database.
lessons.openQuestion: Why might keeping your 'people' and 'companies' in separate folders actually make your AI agent smarter at connecting them?

lessons.title: The Brain-Agent Loop: Read, Respond, Remember
lessons.learningFocus: Trace the complete signal-to-brain data pipeline and explain why reading from the brain BEFORE responding produces better answers than generating from context alone.
lessons.openQuestion: If you always had to search your memories before answering a question, how would your conversations change — and what would you accidentally leave behind?

modules.title: Why gbrain Uses the Compiled Truth Pattern?

lessons.title: The Timeline as Immutable Evidence Chain
lessons.learningFocus: Demonstrate why timeline entries can never be edited or deleted, and explain how every claim in compiled truth must trace back to specific timeline evidence.
lessons.openQuestion: In a world where you can never delete or edit anything you've said, how would your communication habits evolve — and what errors would you have to live with?

lessons.title: Synthesis vs. Evidence: The Psychology of Understanding
lessons.learningFocus: Contrast the two-layer page architecture and explain why timeline entries require explicit API calls while relationship links are auto-reconciled.
lessons.openQuestion: Why do we trust Wikipedia's current article more than its edit history, yet need that history to trust the article at all?

lessons.title: Why Markdown Wins as Source of Truth
lessons.learningFocus: Parse YAML frontmatter from markdown files and explain the benefits of a slug-based API that remains portable across different storage backends.
lessons.openQuestion: If your knowledge could outlive any single app or database, what format would you store it in — and what would you sacrifice for that longevity?

modules.title: How Does gbrain Store and Retrieve Knowledge?

lessons.title: BrainEngine: One Interface, Many Backends
lessons.learningFocus: Describe how the BrainEngine abstraction allows swapping between embedded PGLite and cloud Postgres without changing consumer code.
lessons.openQuestion: What would it mean for your knowledge system if you could run it on your laptop today and migrate to the cloud tomorrow without changing a line of application code?

lessons.title: The Iron Law: Every Mention Creates a Back-Link
lessons.learningFocus: Explain how the auto-link post-hook on put_page extracts entity references and maintains bidirectional relationships without manual link management.
lessons.openQuestion: If every time you mentioned someone in conversation, they automatically knew about it and could respond, how would that change what you say — and to whom?

lessons.title: Sync States and Federation: When Knowledge Becomes Available
lessons.learningFocus: Demonstrate why writes must sync before cross-source queries can see them, and how federation policies govern whether sources share or isolate their content.
lessons.openQuestion: In a world where your personal notes, work projects, and public research live in the same system, what boundaries would you draw — and what would you risk mixing?

modules.title: How Does gbrain Handle Updates and Changes?

lessons.title: APPEND vs REWRITE: The Two Operations That Matter
lessons.learningFocus: Execute APPEND actions to add immutable timeline entries and REWRITE actions to update compiled truth, understanding when each operation is appropriate.
lessons.openQuestion: How do you update your opinion of someone when you can't erase your first impression — and what does that say about how trust is built?

lessons.title: The RESOLVER: Automatic Filing and Tiered Enrichment
lessons.learningFocus: Configure resolver rules to automatically categorize entities and apply appropriate enrichment tiers based on interaction significance.
lessons.openQuestion: If you could only deeply research 10% of the people you meet, what signals would tell you who deserves that investment — and who might you overlook?

lessons.title: Migrations: Evolving Your Brain Without Breaking It
lessons.learningFocus: Orchestrate version-specific migrations including schema updates, skill reloading, and data repairs while persisting update state across sessions.
lessons.openQuestion: How do you rebuild the foundation of a house while people are still living in it — and what promises must you keep to those residents?

modules.title: Who Does the Work in a gbrain System?

lessons.title: Async Sub-Agents: Speed Through Parallelism
lessons.learningFocus: Design async sub-agent patterns that separate data collection from LLM judgment to prevent blocking the main conversation thread.
lessons.openQuestion: If you could delegate your research to a team that works while you sleep, what would you ask them to find — and how would you verify they got it right?

lessons.title: Model Selection: Sonnet for Detection, Opus for Judgment
lessons.learningFocus: Calculate cost differences between models and implement detection pipelines that use cheaper models for pattern matching while reserving expensive models for reasoning.
lessons.openQuestion: When is 'good enough' actually better than 'perfect' — and how do you know which situations deserve your best effort versus your efficient effort?

lessons.title: Shell Jobs and Health Checks: Keeping the System Honest
lessons.learningFocus: Configure shell jobs with proper validation constraints and define DSL-based health checks that audit configurations without slowing the main system.
lessons.openQuestion: How do you build guardrails that catch your mistakes without becoming so restrictive that you stop taking risks — and where is that line?

modules.title: When Should You Use gbrain in Production?

lessons.title: Building Your Personal Mini-AGI: The Skillpack Pattern
lessons.learningFocus: Compose benefit-focused upgrade messages and configure quiet hours to build production agent systems that respect user attention and preferences.
lessons.openQuestion: If your AI assistant was truly yours — trained on your knowledge, respecting your rhythms — what would you let it do, and what would you never delegate?

lessons.title: Disaster Recovery: When Things Go Wrong
lessons.learningFocus: Execute truncated wiki article recovery procedures that rebuild graph relationships by scanning content for entity references.
lessons.openQuestion: When your external memory becomes corrupted, do you trust your internal memory to reconstruct it — or have you outsourced so much that you no longer can?
